source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 21: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer: For scenario variant 21, assume the calculator is available, model/policy versions and tool traces can be logged, and correctness labels are independently reviewable. Treat a call as unnecessary only when the task can be answered correctly without external arithmetic; retain tool use for precision-sensitive, ambiguous, or verification-required cases. Log request class and difficulty, model/policy version, call count and rationale, expression, result/error, tool and end-to-end wall time in milliseconds, token/cost estimate, final correctness, abstention, retries, and recovery. Report unnecessary-call rate, tool success/error rate, final correctness, trajectory length, p50/p95/p99 latency, cost, and recovery, stratified by task type and difficulty with confidence intervals. Falsifiable hypothesis: on a locked held-out set, a stop/no-tool gate reduces unnecessary calls by at least 30% and p95 end-to-end latency by at least 10% while final correctness is non-inferior within 1 percentage point; otherwise do not ship it. Randomize matched requests between the current policy and the gate, tune thresholds only on disjoint development data, and use paired bootstrap intervals with pre-registered non-inferiority and latency tests. Evaluate separate no-tool and tool-needed boundary suites, including precision and ambiguity cases; preference/reward data should penalize needless calls but reward correct tool use, calibrated abstention, and recovery. Control for request mix, cache state, queueing, outages, retries, concurrency, and prompt/model changes; report missing traces and selection effects. Enforce privacy-minimized traces, access controls, and a quality gate that blocks rollout on correctness or safety regressions. Begin with a reversible canary, monitor call rate, error rate, correctness, latency, and recovery, and roll back on the pre-specified guardrail breach or unexplained drift. These are provisional engineering criteria and require domain-expert review.
